Design: a hand-written greedy-with-danger-override policy. First-layer tanh units act as thresholded binary features: “is there gold to the right/left/above/below the player?” using large super-increasing column/row weights, plus row-gated current-row gold-direction units. Other units detect “player in row r and row r contains an enemy”, whether the player is pinned to the top/bottom in-bounds row, and whether enemies exist above/below. Second-layer tanh units form a horizontal gold pull, a vertical gold pull, a current-row danger signal, up/down escape signals that are inhibited at the vertical bounds, and a weak “prefer the side with fewer enemies” safety signal. Output logits make gold pull the chosen axis, give a large bonus to leaving an enemy-occupied row, penalize no-op/left/right/fire while danger is present, and make fire effectively never sampled. Skip fire/gauge channels; fire is only a no-op in this game.
